clue.text: Well you won't need this!

parts.note: 'Well' reads as an interjection, but it means healthy: a person in good health has no use for the remedy a doctor prescribes

explanation.surface: Someone dismissively tells another that a thing is unnecessary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' looks like a filler word opening a remark; read it as 'in good health' and the clue describes what only the sick need.
explanation.definitionFit: Remedies and drugs are taken by the ill, so a healthy person goes without them.

clue.text: Possibly McRae has high place as cartographer

indicators.note: possibly means McRae's letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill or high point, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A man named McRae, perhaps lofty, works as a mapmaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges MCRAE into MERCA, followed by TOR. Mercator devised the map projection named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerardus Mercator was a Flemish mapmaker famous for his map projection.

clue.text: Explosive takes effect in a second

definitions.text: Explosive takes effect in a second

parts.words: Explosive takes effect in a second
parts.note: describes the small charge that sets off a larger explosion almost instantly

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the device that sets off a bomb in an instant.
explanation.definitionFit: A detonator is the device that triggers a main explosive charge.

clue.text: Schoolmaster gives strokes of course !

definitions.meaning: Mr ... is the gentle schoolmaster of James Hilton's novel Goodbye, Mr ...
short lofted shots played on a golf course

explanation.walkthrough: 'course' is a golf course, not 'of course' meaning naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilton's novel Goodbye, Mr Chips is about a schoolteacher; and short lofted golf shots onto the green are chips.

clue.text: Book to see glamorous actor

parts.note: a novel is a book
lo is an old word meaning look or see

explanation.surface: Read a book in order to see a film star.
explanation.walkthrough: Ivor Novello was a Welsh matinee idol and composer of the 1920s to 1940s.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivor Novello was a handsome stage and screen star and songwriter.

clue.text: Meal supplier returns cash by morning

indicators.note: returns means the joined words for cash and morning are read backwards as one run

parts.note: a coin is a piece of cash
AM is the abbreviation for morning, ante meridiem

explanation.surface: A grain merchant pays back money before noon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns the whole run COINAM back to front, giving the plant name.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassava, also called manioc, is a plant whose root is ground into a starchy flour or meal.

clue.text: Like someone surrounding one with calumny

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of

indicators.note: surrounding means the word for someone goes round the letter for one

parts.note: a person is someone
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Like a person who besets another with slander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounding' puts I inside PERSON, giving PERSION after AS.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspersion is a slanderous remark that attacks someone's reputation.

clue.text: Jones takes the "d" out of " dye"

indicators.note: the clue says outright that a letter D is removed from the dye's name

parts.note: indigo is a deep blue dye

explanation.surface: A man named Jones removes a letter from a word.
explanation.walkthrough: Inigo Jones was the English architect of the Banqueting House in Whitehall; 'Jones' defines him by his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Inigo Jones was the seventeenth-century English architect who brought Palladian style to Britain.

clue.text: Requirements of anglers and many others

definitions.text: Requirements of anglers and many others

parts.words: Requirements of anglers and many others
parts.note: names the wicker baskets that anglers carry their catch in, also used by fishwives and lobstermen

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes a piece of fishing gear also used by others who carry fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A creel is a wicker basket for carrying fish.

clue.text: Right sort of support ?

parts.note: alludes to the saying 'as right as' this three-legged stand, which never wobbles

explanation.walkthrough: The British saying 'right as a trivet' means perfectly fine; a three-legged stand is always steady.
explanation.definitionFit: A trivet is a three-legged stand for a pot or kettle.

clue.text: Dog worries terrier about quarter to five

indicators.note: about means the shuffled letters go round the pair that follows
worries means the letters of terrier are harried into a new order

parts.note: E, east, is one of the four quarters of the compass
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A dog harasses a terrier at a quarter to five in the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worries' rearranges TERRIER into RETRIER; 'about' puts it round EV, read as 'quarter to five', E then V. The time of day is a false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: A retriever is a breed of gun dog trained to fetch shot game.

clue.text: Lions in the morning mist

definitions.meaning: a group of lions is called a ...
'... of the morning' is an old phrase for a mist or light shower at sunrise

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense comes from the phrase 'pride of the morning', a dawn mist taken as the promise of a fine day.
explanation.definitionFit: A family group of big cats is a pride; and the dawn haze called 'pride of the morning' gives the second sense.

clue.text: Miss Wickfield returns some chap's engagement ring

indicators.note: returns means the run found in the words is read backwards
some means only part of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: A young lady gives back the ring a man gave her when they got engaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks SENGA from chap'S ENGAgement, and 'returns' turns it round. Agnes Wickfield is the heroine David marries in Dickens's David Copperfield.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnes Wickfield is the character in Dickens's David Copperfield whom the hero finally marries.

clue.text: City organ transplant centre ?

parts.note: the liver is an organ of the body
a pool is a central stock shared out, as organs for transplant are held in a common supply

explanation.surface: A hospital in a city where organs are transplanted.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one medical phrase; split it as an organ plus a shared supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Liverpool is a large port city in north-west England.

clue.text: N.A.T.O. scheme connected with port and lake

indicators.note: scheme means the letters of N.A.T.O. are arranged into a fresh plan

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port, often called just Rio

explanation.surface: A NATO plan involving a harbour and a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scheme' rearranges NATO into ONTA, which is then joined by RIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Ontario is one of the five Great Lakes of North America.

clue.text: Pondered having drink with diet — an odd scheme

parts.note: rum is a drink

indicators.note: odd scheme means the letters of diet and an are arranged in a strange pattern

explanation.surface: Someone thought over a plan to drink while dieting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd scheme' rearranges DIET and AN into INATED, which follows RUM. 'vice,' in the held text is not on the printed page.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruminate is to think deeply, chewing over a matter.

clue.text: Very heavy gasteropod ?

definitions.meaning: split as ..., three tons, which is very heavy indeed
a large sea snail, a gastropod with a long spiral shell

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a pun: break the word into TRI (three) and TON. Gasteropod is an old spelling of gastropod.
explanation.definitionFit: A triton is a marine snail, a kind of mollusc; and tri-ton sounds like three tons, a crushing weight.

clue.text: Age in choice of working

indicators.note: in means the age goes inside the word for choice

parts.note: an option is a choice
an era is an age

explanation.surface: Age is an option for someone at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts ERA inside OPTION after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine in operation is functioning, so the noun names the state of running.

clue.text: Walks unsteadily, to fall into the vessel

indicators.note: into means the word for falling goes inside the vessel's letters

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the usual prefix for a vessel
to tumble is to fall

explanation.surface: Someone lurches about and topples into a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts TUMBLE inside SS.
explanation.definitionFit: To stumble is to trip or walk with faltering steps.

clue.text: A sky-sign is Dumas's creation

parts.note: the Ram, Aries, is a sign of the zodiac seen in the sky

explanation.surface: An advertising sign in the sky is said to be a French novelist's invention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sky-sign' looks like a neon advertisement but is a zodiac sign, the Ram. Aramis is one of the Three Musketeers.
explanation.definitionFit: Aramis is one of the musketeers in Alexandre Dumas's novel The Three Musketeers.

clue.text: Comes in as advised at eleven, sober

annotationWithheld.why: Comes in as advised at eleven, sober (6): SEDATE; no parse found for 'Comes in as advised at eleven' as wordplay for SEDATE
annotationWithheld.clue: Comes in as advised at eleven, sober

clue.text: Satisfied with a French tale, not without love

parts.note: conte is French for a story or tale

indicators.note: without means the letter for love is dropped from the word before it

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone is pleased with a French story that is full of romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes O (love) from NOT, leaving NT to follow CONTE. 'not without love' reads as a double negative meaning romantic.
explanation.definitionFit: Being pleased and wanting nothing more is to be content.

clue.text: Against taking a kind partner

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
a sort is a kind

explanation.surface: Someone opposed to taking a nice spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kind' looks like an adjective (a kind partner) but is the noun meaning sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A consort is a spouse, especially of a reigning monarch.

clue.text: Business intrigue ?

definitions.meaning: an ... is a matter or concern, as in 'my ...'

explanation.definitionFit: A matter of concern is an affair; and so is a clandestine romance.

clue.text: Scholar travelling in Berks?

parts.note: faring is an old word for travelling, as in wayfaring
a don is a university teacher or scholar

explanation.surface: An academic on a journey through Berkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Faringdon is a market town that was in Berkshire (Berks), an English county, when this was set; the question mark admits the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Faringdon is a town in the Vale of White Horse, historically part of Berkshire.

clue.text: Knocks about Minehead looking for swindles

indicators.note: about means the word for knocks goes round the head of mine

parts.note: raps are knocks
read as 'mine head', the first letter of mine; Minehead is also a Somerset seaside town

explanation.surface: Someone wanders round the Somerset resort of Minehead looking for frauds.
explanation.walkthrough: Minehead is a seaside town in Somerset, but here split as the head of 'mine', M, which RAPS goes round.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramps is old slang for swindles or rackets.

clue.text: True gentleman of French province

parts.note: real means true or genuine
M is the abbreviation for monsieur, a French gentleman

explanation.surface: A genuine Frenchman from the provinces.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a kingdom or domain, a region ruled or governed.

clue.text: Incur debts before delivery?

definitions.meaning: to ... a bill is to incur debts
in cricket the ... is the bowler's approach before delivering the ball

explanation.walkthrough: Cricket: the bowler's run-up comes before the delivery of the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Accumulating a bill is to run it up; and a bowler's approach to the crease is the run-up.

clue.text: A retired doctor has something to concede

indicators.note: retired means the doctor's letters go back the way they came

parts.note: MD is a Doctor of Medicine
it can stand for an unnamed thing, as in 'there's something about it'

explanation.surface: An old doctor in retirement has something to own up to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns MD round to DM, placed between A and IT.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit a point is to grant or confess that it is true.

clue.text: Prickly ascent for the artist

parts.note: a thorn is a prickle, so it stands for prickly
a hill is a slope one ascends

explanation.surface: A painter climbs a thorny slope.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir James Thornhill painted the dome of St Paul's Cathedral and the Painted Hall at Greenwich.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir James Thornhill was an English baroque painter of murals and ceilings.

clue.text: About two-thirds of 20 would be pale green

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: two-thirds of means four of the six letters are kept and the last two dropped

parts.note: the answer to 20 down is a word meaning sober, calm

explanation.surface: A colour described as roughly two-thirds of another answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two-thirds of' keeps SEDA from SEDATE (20 down), which follows RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Reseda is a greyish-green colour named after the mignonette plant.

clue.text: Bob goes to extremes, collecting salaries

annotationWithheld.why: Bob goes to extremes, collecting salaries (8): STIPENDS; no parse found that uses every word (S for bob, TIP and ENDS, and 'collecting' do not combine without a word doing two jobs or left over)
annotationWithheld.clue: Bob goes to extremes, collecting salaries
